C1.rationale: Constraints are proportionate: no dense MUST/NEVER prohibitions, and the hard ones are contract-shaped (stop on --check-only, gate writes on --fix or user confirmation). It falls short of exemplary because several constraints restate what a capable model would do anyway (the Error Handling rows telling it to skip dependency auditing with no package manager, or skip SAST for an unsupported CodeQL language) and no constraint says why, so the model cannot generalise past the enumerated cases.

C2.rationale: The interface is self-describing: the --type alternatives are enumerated inline at the point of declaration in both args and argument-hint, and a Parameters section names each flag's effect, so the examples illustrate rather than define. It stops short of 5 because the contradictory --check-only + --fix combination is neither made impossible nor named, and the Agentic Optimizations rows mostly restate one flag each rather than resolving genuine ambiguity.

C3.rationale: Detail is genuinely deferred: the ten execution steps stay one-liners and every template, report format, and standards block is loaded on demand, while the detection logic runs as a bundled script that never enters context at all. It is not a 5 because all deferred material sits in one ~13KB REFERENCE.md spanning dependency, SAST, secrets, policy, CI, and report content, so a run touching only Step 4 still pulls the whole sidecar rather than a path-specific file.

C4.rationale: Overlapping material is mostly pointed at rather than copied — REFERENCE.md owns every template and the See Also block names /configure:pre-commit and /configure:workflows as the owners of adjacent guidance. It is not higher because Step 6 restates gitleaks install commands and .gitleaks.toml/pre-commit-hook setup that git-plugin/skills/git-security-checks/SKILL.md already owns (same brew/go install pair, same .gitleaks.toml allowlist duty), and that skill is never named as the owner.

C5.rationale: C5 applies only to always-loaded surfaces (CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules/*). This is a SKILL.md body that costs tokens only once the skill fires.

C6.rationale: The deterministic half is a real artifact, not prose: language/posture detection is a runnable script whose structured output contract is named field-by-field, and the unit is explicit about which artifact to run versus which to read. It misses 5 because Step 1 asks the model to hand-check six release pages via WebSearch/WebFetch every run — mechanical, repeatable lookup described in prose where the same script (or a pin file) could state it exactly.

evidence.quote: Parse `STATUS=` and the `ISSUES:` block from the output.

top_finding: Fold Step 1's six-link manual version lookup into the detection script (or drop it in favour of a pinned version list) so the one remaining block of mechanical work stops being re-derived in prose on every invocation.
counter_finding: Step 2's script invocation plus its named STATUS=/ISSUES:/KEY=VALUE output contract earns its tokens outright — it replaces an entire prose detection procedure with a deterministic artifact the model runs rather than reads.

house_standards_seen: CLAUDE.md (project instructions, incl. plugin lifecycle and rules index)
leakage.note: The three files on the do-not-read list (skill-quality.md, skill-development.md, skill-evaluation.md) were injected into my context by the harness before my first turn; I did not open them and did not score against them. The excluded house criteria are visibly present in this unit (a When to Use table, an Agentic Optimizations table, a REFERENCE.md by that exact filename, date frontmatter) and I awarded no credit or penalty for any of them: C3's 4 rests on the executable script plus on-demand deferral, and its cap rests on the sidecar being monolithic, not on any char threshold; C2's 4 rests on the enumerated --type alternatives, not on argument-hint being present per house convention.
